items.title: The water cycle

steps.label: Evaporation
steps.detail: the sun heats water in oceans and lakes

steps.label: Condensation
steps.detail: water vapour cools and forms clouds

steps.label: Precipitation
steps.detail: water falls as rain, snow or hail

steps.label: Runoff
steps.detail: water flows over land into rivers

steps.label: Collection
steps.detail: water gathers in oceans, lakes and underground

points: The diagram shows the water cycle, a continuous natural process with five stages.
First, the sun heats water in oceans and lakes, and it evaporates into the air as vapour.
Then the vapour cools and condenses into clouds, after which the water falls back to earth as rain, snow or hail.
After that, the water runs off the land into rivers and finally collects in oceans, lakes and underground, where it evaporates again.
Overall, the same water moves endlessly between the land, the sea and the sky.

items.title: The life cycle of a frog

steps.label: Frogspawn
steps.detail: the female lays clusters of eggs in water

steps.label: Tadpole
steps.detail: larvae hatch and breathe through gills

steps.label: Tadpole with legs
steps.detail: back legs grow, then front legs

steps.label: Froglet
steps.detail: the tail shrinks and lungs develop

steps.label: Adult frog
steps.detail: the frog lives on land and breeds

points: The diagram illustrates the life cycle of a frog, which has five main stages.
It begins when the female lays frogspawn, clusters of eggs, in water.
Then tadpoles hatch and breathe through gills, and after that they grow back legs followed by front legs.
Next, the young animal becomes a froglet as its tail shrinks and lungs develop, and finally it becomes an adult frog, which lays eggs and starts the cycle again.
In conclusion, the frog changes dramatically in form as it moves from life in water to life on land.

items.title: Recycling plastic bottles

steps.label: Collection
steps.detail: used bottles are gathered from recycling bins

steps.label: Sorting
steps.detail: bottles are separated by type of plastic

steps.label: Washing
steps.detail: labels and dirt are removed

steps.label: Shredding
steps.detail: bottles are cut into small flakes

steps.label: Melting
steps.detail: flakes are melted and formed into pellets

steps.label: Manufacturing
steps.detail: pellets are made into new bottles

steps.label: Use
steps.detail: consumers buy and use the new bottles

points: The diagram shows how plastic bottles are recycled in a loop of seven stages.
First, used bottles are collected from recycling bins and sorted according to the type of plastic.
Then they are washed to remove labels and dirt, shredded into small flakes, and melted to form pellets.
After that, the pellets are used to manufacture new bottles, which consumers buy and use, and finally these are collected again, so the process returns to the start.
Overall, the process turns waste back into new products instead of sending it to landfill.

items.title: The carbon cycle

steps.label: Atmosphere
steps.detail: carbon dioxide is held in the air

steps.label: Photosynthesis
steps.detail: plants absorb carbon dioxide to make food

steps.label: Feeding
steps.detail: animals eat plants and take in carbon

steps.label: Death and decay
steps.detail: decomposers break down dead plants and animals

steps.label: Respiration and burning
steps.detail: carbon dioxide is released back into the air

points: The diagram shows the carbon cycle, which is made up of five connected stages.
It begins with carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, which plants absorb during photosynthesis to make their food.
Then animals take in this carbon by eating the plants, and when plants and animals die, decomposers break them down.
Finally, respiration and the burning of fuels release carbon dioxide back into the air, completing the cycle.
In short, carbon constantly moves between the atmosphere and living things.

items.title: How chocolate is made

steps.label: Harvesting
steps.detail: ripe cocoa pods are cut from the trees

steps.label: Fermentation
steps.detail: beans are left to ferment for several days

steps.label: Drying
steps.detail: beans are spread out to dry in the sun

steps.label: Roasting
steps.detail: beans are roasted to develop their flavour

steps.label: Grinding
steps.detail: shells are removed and nibs ground into paste

steps.label: Mixing
steps.detail: sugar and milk are added and mixed

steps.label: Moulding
steps.detail: chocolate is tempered, poured into moulds and cooled

points: The diagram illustrates how chocolate is produced, in seven stages from the farm to the finished bar.
First, ripe cocoa pods are harvested, and the beans are fermented for several days and then dried in the sun.
After that, the beans are roasted to develop their flavour, their shells are removed, and the inner nibs are ground into a paste.
Next, sugar and milk are mixed in, and finally the chocolate is tempered, poured into moulds and cooled into bars.
Overall, it is a long process that turns a raw agricultural crop into a manufactured food.

items.title: How a bill becomes law

steps.label: Drafting
steps.detail: a proposed law is written as a bill

steps.label: First reading
steps.detail: the bill is formally introduced in parliament

steps.label: Second reading
steps.detail: members debate the main principles of the bill

steps.label: Committee stage
steps.detail: the bill is examined in detail and amended

steps.label: Third reading
steps.detail: a final debate and vote take place

steps.label: Second chamber
steps.detail: the other house reviews the bill

steps.label: Assent
steps.detail: the head of state signs it into law

points: The diagram shows the seven stages through which a bill becomes law in a typical parliament.
First, the proposed law is drafted as a bill and then formally introduced at the first reading.
Then members debate its main principles at the second reading, after which a committee examines it in detail and makes amendments.
Next, there is a final vote at the third reading, the second chamber reviews the bill, and finally the head of state gives assent, so it becomes law.
In conclusion, a bill is checked and debated several times before it can become law.

items.title: Making bricks

steps.label: Digging
steps.detail: clay is dug from the ground

steps.label: Mixing
steps.detail: clay is mixed with sand and water

steps.label: Moulding
steps.detail: the mixture is shaped in moulds or cut

steps.label: Drying
steps.detail: bricks are dried to remove moisture

steps.label: Firing
steps.detail: bricks are baked at high temperature in a kiln

steps.label: Cooling
steps.detail: bricks are left to cool slowly

steps.label: Delivery
steps.detail: bricks are packaged and sent to customers

points: The diagram shows how bricks are manufactured, in seven stages.
First, clay is dug from the ground and then mixed with sand and water.
After that, the mixture is shaped in moulds or cut into blocks, and the bricks are dried to remove moisture.
Next, they are fired at a high temperature in a kiln and cooled slowly, and finally they are packaged and delivered to customers.
Overall, the process turns a raw natural material into a finished building product.

items.title: Generating electricity from coal

steps.label: Coal delivery
steps.detail: mined coal arrives at the power station

steps.label: Pulverising
steps.detail: coal is crushed into a fine powder

steps.label: Boiler
steps.detail: burning coal boils water into steam

steps.label: Turbine
steps.detail: high pressure steam spins a turbine

steps.label: Generator
steps.detail: the turbine drives a generator to produce electricity

steps.label: Transformer
steps.detail: the voltage is increased for transmission

steps.label: Power grid
steps.detail: electricity reaches homes and businesses

points: The diagram illustrates how electricity is generated in a coal-fired power station, in seven stages.
First, mined coal is delivered to the station and crushed into a fine powder.
Then the coal is burnt in a boiler, which turns water into high pressure steam, and this steam spins a turbine connected to a generator.
After that, a transformer increases the voltage, and finally the electricity is carried through the grid to homes and businesses.
In short, the chemical energy in coal is converted into heat, then movement, and finally electricity.

items.title: Publishing academic research

steps.label: Research
steps.detail: a study is carried out and analysed

steps.label: Writing
steps.detail: the researchers write up their findings

steps.label: Submission
steps.detail: the paper is sent to a journal

steps.label: Peer review
steps.detail: experts assess the quality of the work

steps.label: Revision
steps.detail: authors respond to the reviewers' comments

steps.label: Acceptance
steps.detail: the editor accepts the revised paper

steps.label: Publication
steps.detail: the article appears in print or online

points: The diagram shows the seven stages involved in publishing academic research.
First, researchers carry out a study, analyse the results and write up their findings as a paper.
Then the paper is submitted to a journal, where it goes through peer review by experts in the field.
After that, the authors revise the paper in response to the comments, the editor accepts it, and finally it is published in print or online.
Overall, the process includes several quality checks before research reaches its readers.

items.title: Treating drinking water

steps.label: Intake
steps.detail: water is drawn from a river or reservoir

steps.label: Screening
steps.detail: large debris such as leaves is removed

steps.label: Coagulation
steps.detail: chemicals make small particles clump together

steps.label: Sedimentation
steps.detail: heavy clumps settle to the bottom

steps.label: Filtration
steps.detail: water passes through layers of sand and gravel

steps.label: Disinfection
steps.detail: chlorine is added to kill harmful microorganisms

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: clean water is piped to homes

points: The diagram illustrates how water is treated to make it safe to drink, in seven stages.
First, water is drawn from a river or reservoir and screened to remove large debris such as leaves.
Then chemicals are added so that small particles clump together, and these heavy clumps settle to the bottom during sedimentation.
After that, the water is filtered through sand and gravel and disinfected with chlorine, and finally it is piped to homes.
In conclusion, the water is cleaned in several stages, each removing smaller impurities than the last.
